item.text:
**Bottom line**: Xi’s 2024 record is not “slogans only.” I found several concrete implementation signals in budgeting, housing stabilization, healthcare reform, and administrative service rollout. The limiting factor is that much of the state’s reach still runs through Party control and coercive governance, and some flagship measures looked only partially effective.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 2024 government work report highlights | State Council / China.org.cn | 2024-03-05 | https://www.china.org.cn/chinese/2024-03/14/content_117057714.htm | The 2024 work report set concrete targets and funding: 3.9 trillion yuan in local special-purpose bonds, 1 trillion yuan in ultra-long treasury bonds, 700 billion yuan in central investment, and explicit goals on jobs, domestic demand, and risk defusing. This is strong evidence of declarations being translated into a budgeted program. | 8B.6 |
| China grants over 200 bln yuan from central budget for investment | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-04-17 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202404/17/content_WS661fc4dfc6d0868f4e8e62d3.html | By mid-April, more than 200 billion yuan had already been allocated, with the funds tied to project supervision and to 15,000 projects funded by the 2023 treasury allocation. This shows actual administrative deployment, not just rhetoric. | 8B.6 |
| China to deepen medical, healthcare reform in 2024 | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-06-24 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202406/24/content_WS6678b249c6d0868f4e8e8776.html | The health system announced specific 2024 reforms: better primary-care access, lower patient costs, expanded bulk drug procurement, and pilots for price reform in three provinces. That is observable implementation with named mechanisms. | 8B.6 |
| China releases list of new priorities for one-stop government services in 2024 | State Council / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-07-19 | https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202407/19/content_WS669a3159c6d0868f4e8e9448.html | The State Council issued a priority list for one-stop services, including medical reimbursement, housing-related services, veteran services, and overseas-student services, and told agencies to standardize rollout and share data. This is concrete state-capacity building. | 8B.6 |
| China unveils new property support measures amid concerns about Evergrande fallout | Reuters | 2024-01-31 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-unveils-new-property-support-measures-amid-concerns-about-evergrande-fallout-3287774 | Beijing and state-backed actors had already moved into operational stabilization: whitelist lending, eased home-buying curbs, and a policy push to revive the property sector. This is real intervention, not symbolic signaling. | 8B.6 |
| China’s latest property market support package - its contents and what’s at stake | Reuters | 2024-05-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/explainerchinas-latest-property-market-support-package--its-contents-and-whats-at-stake-3455636 | The May package cut downpayment requirements, lowered mortgage-rate floors, and created a 300 billion yuan relending facility for SOE purchases of unsold homes. That shows concrete implementation, though still within a heavily managed system. | 8B.6 |
| China’s property support measures disappoint, developers’ shares falter | Reuters | 2024-05-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/most-chinese-developers-shares-fall-despite-latest-support-measures-3447284 | Markets judged the “historic” property steps insufficient for a sustainable turnaround. This is counterevidence to any claim that the leadership had fully converted its housing promises into effective results. | 8B.6 |
| US-funded Radio Free Asia shuts Hong Kong bureau, citing security law concerns | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157 | The Article 23 security law produced an observable chilling effect: RFA closed its Hong Kong bureau over staff-safety concerns after authorities labeled it a “foreign force.” This shows state reach in practice, but as coercive control rather than a benign policy promise. | 8B.6 |
| China’s Xi says army faces “deep-seated” problems in anti-corruption drive | Reuters | 2024-06-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/chinas-xi-says-army-faces-deepseated-problems-in-anticorruption-drive-3489069 | Xi publicly acknowledged serious internal problems in the military and called for rectification during an ongoing purge. This supports the view that some declarations became enforcement, but it also shows the system still required repeated cleanup. | 8B.6 |

**Search gap**
- I found strong sectoral evidence of implementation, but not an independent 2024 audit showing Xi personally converted declarations into outcomes across the whole state.
- The evidence base is mostly official policy issuance plus Reuters-style reporting on selected sectors, so it is stronger on “the state acted” than on “the stated goal was fully achieved.”
- I also did not find a reliable 2024 source proving that the more democratic or accountable-sounding declarations were matched by meaningful institutional openness; the clearest counterevidence runs the other way through censorship, security law enforcement, and Party centralization.
